name: Corp Criadh

a clay doll stuck with pins or cut, then placed in a stream
running water slowly dissolved the clay

okr.objective: Corp Criadh is a Scottish ritual clay object used to work ill on others.
key_results: People in the Highlands used Corp Criadh until the 19th century.
Craftspeople stuck the doll with pins or cut it, then placed it in a stream so the water dissolved the clay.
The intended victim died when the doll dissolved, unless someone saw it first and broke the spell.
okr.evidence: Henderson, George. Survivals in Belief Among the Celts. Glasgow: James MacLeose and Sons, 1911, 16.

text: Corp Criadh, also Corp Creagh, is a ritual article of Scottish use. Highlanders kept working with such clay dolls long into the 1800s. A maker shaped a figure to injure a neighbor or repay a straying lover, then pierced or sliced the model and left it afloat in a stream. The running water ate the clay away little by little. When it had wholly vanished, the one hated at a distance suffered those wounds and perished. If a bystander saw the doll before the charm ended, its force broke and the victim recovered. George Henderson set the matter down in 1911 in his study of beliefs that linger among the Celtic.
